title: Decode CTC with a beam, a language model, and hotwords
brief: Build greedy decoding and CTC prefix beam search, check the beam against brute-force enumeration, then add shallow fusion with a character bigram model and a hotword bonus.
hints: greedy_decode: np.argmax(log_probs, axis=1) gives the path. Walk it once, keeping a symbol when it differs from the previous frame's symbol and is not the blank.

prefix_beam_search keeps two numbers per prefix because a repeated label means two different things: after a blank it starts a new copy (use p_b), and straight after the same label it merges into the old one (use p_nb).
Accumulate with np.logaddexp into a defaultdict whose default is (-inf, -inf). Rank by np.logaddexp(p_b, p_nb) plus the extra prefix score, and keep the top beam_width.
train_char_bigram: start each text with previous = 0, count counts[previous, current], zero column 0, add the smoothing to columns 1 and up, and divide each row by its sum.
hotword_score: count complete occurrences with a sliding window, and find the longest partial match by comparing prefix[-k:] with word[:k] for k from 1 to len(word) - 1.
